dedupe_keys.name: short term load forecasting for non residential buildings contrasting artificial occupancy attributes

description: Massana i Raurich, Joaquim and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The documented support-vector regression method predicts hourly electricity consumption using calculated occupancy indicators, including forecasts months ahead. It compares artificial occupancy attributes ranging from simple calendar information to detailed activity information, showing that additional complexity does not necessarily improve predictions. The demonstration covers University of Girona non-residential buildings and explicitly links the enriched 2011–2014 data deposit. Related thesis and energy-service papers describe the broader modelling programme; identical model versions are not asserted. The source establishes an implemented forecasting formulation but does not identify an open code distribution in the inspected metadata. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
